reality_delta: The task was to update a planning document, which is inherently a documentation change, so a 'reality change' here means the plan file actually contains the claimed new section with the right structure and content. The request only asserts this; it does not provide the actual text, diff, hash, or post-edit verification, so the change is not independently verifiable.
main_concern: The review is asked to accept that section 2.2.3 was added and correctly separates closed/open residual items, but the only evidence is a summary and lifecycle metadata. A plan file reference and a passed gate are not proof that the claimed content is in the file or that it accurately reflects the current residual state.
top_risks: The new section may not exist, may be empty, or may not actually list the claimed closed/next-priority/open items.
Status-update rules requiring evidence files may be stated but not applied consistently because the plan provides no enforcement mechanism or owner.
Future work may treat this plan refresh as implicit progress toward RSP implementation despite the 'no implementation' constraint.
missing_evidence: A verbatim excerpt or diff of the added section 2.2.3 showing the actual closed, next-priority, and still-open items.
A post-edit validation result (e.g., lifecycle check, file hash, or grep output) proving the file contains the claimed content.
A clear mapping from each listed residual item to its originating issue or previous todo so the baseline can be audited.
minimum_fix: Provide the actual diff or a quoted excerpt of section 2.2.3, plus a post-edit verification command (e.g., lifecycle check, sha256, or structured grep) that confirms the new content is present. Do not treat the plan refresh itself as closure of any residual item.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The next cycle must start by showing the concrete file content, not by asserting 'the plan now covers it.' If gaps remain, produce a plan patch, not another status note.
